react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics differential screen strongly implicates the steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism axis across four independent enrichment paradigms. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at rank 2 with FDR 6.04e-18, alongside five SMPDB and WikiPathways analogues including Aromatase deficiency (SMPDB:SMP00565) and the Reactome Estrogen/Androgen biosynthesis modules. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as the top hit (p=5.77e-07), overlapping six steroid input metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct activity scored MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p=8.4e-05) with all 15 steroid hormone compounds mapped in the network, and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as rank 1 (p=1.68e-04). The six driver steroids — 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951), androst-4-ene-3,17-dione (KEGG:C00280), estrone (KEGG:C00468), 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one/DHT (KEGG:C03917), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), and dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227) — converge on the CYP19A1 (aromatase) and HSD3B/CYP17A1 reactions that interconvert androgens and estrogens. Non-steroid hits (N-acetylgalactosamine, coumarin, xanthine, β-mercaptoethanol) were sub-threshold in all paradigms, consistent with background noise or off-target metabolic effects. The convergent signal across ORA (hypergeometric), network activity (Mummichog), and community-standard KEGG PSEA strongly supports a treatment-induced perturbation of the C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism pathway.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The RaMP multi-database over-representation analysis identified KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) as the top-scoring KEGG pathway with FDR 6.05e-18 and fold enrichment 1501, sharing six driver steroids with its SMPDB analogue SMPDB:SMP00068. The Reactome pathway REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) appeared at rank 4 with FDR 5.33e-17, confirming the same six input metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently scored MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit with p=0.000252 and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as rank 1 with p=0.001176, both mapping 14–15 input-compound matches to the C21-steroid network. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 as the sole hit with p=2.25e-08, overlapping all six steroid input metabolites. The convergent signal across ORA, m/z network activity, and KEGG PSEA converges on steroid hormone biosynthesis and interconversion, with 17β-estradiol, estrone, androstenedione, testosterone, DHT, and DHEA as the six driver compounds.

MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as the top hit (p=5.77e-07), overlapping six steroid input metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct activity scored MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p=8.4e-05) with all 15 steroid hormone compounds mapped in the network, and MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as rank 1 (p=1.68e-04). The six driver steroids — 17β-estradiol (KEGG:C00951), androst-4-ene-3,17-dione (KEGG:C00280), estrone (KEGG:C00468), 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one/DHT (KEGG:C03917), testosterone (KEGG:C00535), and dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227) — converge on the CYP19A1 (aromatase) and HSD3B/CYP17A1 reactions that interconvert androgens and estrogens. Non-steroid hits (N-acetylgalactosamine, coumarin, xanthine, β-mercaptoethanol) were sub-threshold in all paradigms, consistent with background noise or off-target metabolic effects. The convergent signal across ORA (hypergeometric), network activity (Mummichog), and community-standard KEGG PSEA strongly supports a treatment-induced perturbation of the C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism pathway.
